chapters.title: Thinking Badly-or Not Thinking at All?
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening failure is recognition failure: pressure arrives as insult, threat, delay, or status friction before the person realizes a thinking moment is happening. The angry CEO warning, ordinary reactive scenes, biology, and the four-default map all point to the same upstream loss.
chapters.coreMove: Catch the instant when a default is about to define the moment before your goal does.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the chapter as generic calm-down advice or a plea to reason better after the reaction has already started.

chapters.title: The Emotion Default
chapters.sourcePressure: Emotion is the first fast default: anger, fear, outrage, urgency, hunger, fatigue, stress, distraction, and unfamiliar settings can possess the moment before facts or goals stabilize it. The Godfather contrast and Steve story show both strategic and irreversible costs.
chapters.coreMove: Treat hot emotion and vulnerable body states as hazard conditions before choosing the next move.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning emotion into a villain or advising suppression instead of diagnosing when feeling has taken command.

chapters.title: The Ego Default
chapters.sourcePressure: Ego is the default that protects self-image, status, rank, and identity before truth or learning gets a vote. The source lane is narrow: status threat, territory, hierarchy, self-preservation, and the border with social pressure.
chapters.coreMove: Name the self-image threat before it converts feedback into defense.
chapters.commonMisread: Making ego a personality insult instead of a repeatable judgment failure under status pressure.

chapters.title: The Social Default
chapters.sourcePressure: Social pressure rewards conformity before truth. This chapter should focus on belonging pressure, group norms, borrowed judgment, and the pause needed before a room's momentum decides for you.
chapters.coreMove: Separate what the group rewards from what the facts support before agreeing.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing social default to teenage peer pressure or treating all group influence as bad.

chapters.title: The Inertia Default
chapters.sourcePressure: Inertia is the default of comfort, habit, familiarity, and change resistance. The chapter contrasts passive continuation with deliberately built clarity-supporting defaults.
chapters.coreMove: Ask what is continuing only because it was already moving.
chapters.commonMisread: Mistaking inertia for laziness or motivation failure instead of familiarity defending itself.

chapters.title: Default to Clarity
chapters.sourcePressure: The pivot from diagnosis to design: build conditions before pressure arrives so space, environment, positioning, and deliberate defaults make clear action easier than reactive action.
chapters.coreMove: Design the next clear response before the next pressured moment asks for it.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating clarity as a mood, value, or motivational preference rather than an engineered default.

chapters.title: Self-Accountability
chapters.sourcePressure: The first strength interrupts autopilot by owning choice, error, contribution, and responsibility before blame or excuse can take over.
chapters.coreMove: Move from what happened to what part you own while the moment is still changeable.
chapters.commonMisread: Making accountability moralistic or blame-heavy instead of operational for better judgment.

chapters.title: Self-Knowledge
chapters.sourcePressure: Self-knowledge makes ownership precise by mapping strengths, weaknesses, edge, and limits so you know where to trust yourself, slow down, or add support.
chapters.coreMove: Locate the edge where your judgment is reliable and the edge where it needs support.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning self-knowledge into broad introspection, personality typing, or self-esteem talk.

chapters.title: Self-Control
chapters.sourcePressure: Self-control protects the accurate map once fear, desire, and pressure start pushing against it. The lane is discipline, fear, desire, emotional regulation, and pressure resistance.
chapters.coreMove: Hold the better standard in place while fear or desire tries to shorten the clock.
chapters.commonMisread: Selling heroic discipline or shame instead of showing restraint as protection for judgment.

chapters.title: Self-Confidence
chapters.sourcePressure: Self-confidence stabilizes independent judgment after self-knowledge and self-control. It is grounded self-trust under social pressure, not ego, charisma, or performance.
chapters.coreMove: Trust your prepared judgment long enough to keep thinking when the room presses back.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing confidence with ego, certainty, charm, or ignoring contrary evidence.

chapters.title: Strength in Action
chapters.sourcePressure: After the four strengths, the chapter moves from internal structure to visible use in ordinary moments: applying strengths, translating them to action, and becoming consistent.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a private standard into a visible behavior before the situation moves on.
chapters.commonMisread: Leaving strengths as self-description rather than making them observable under pressure.

chapters.title: Setting the Standards
chapters.sourcePressure: Standards protect repeated good behavior across time and pressure. The chapter is about rules, thresholds, decision quality, and self-command that reduce avoidable improvisation.
chapters.coreMove: Set the rule before pressure starts negotiating exceptions.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating standards as slogans, perfectionism, or rigid identity claims.

chapters.title: Exemplars + Practice
chapters.sourcePressure: Exemplars and practice make standards more usable through models, rehearsal, calibration, measurement, and simple feedback.
chapters.coreMove: Use a visible model and repeated rehearsal to calibrate what your standard actually looks like.
chapters.commonMisread: Collecting role models for inspiration instead of practicing the specific behavior they make visible.

chapters.title: Knowing Your Weaknesses
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shifts from strengthening standards to mapping vulnerability: blind spots, exposure, recurring failure patterns, and conditions where judgment is least reliable.
chapters.coreMove: Map the conditions where you predictably become less trustworthy to yourself.
chapters.commonMisread: Confession, self-criticism, or generic weakness lists instead of exposure mapping.

chapters.title: Protecting Yourself with Safeguards
chapters.sourcePressure: After naming weak points, build safeguards: rules, guardrails, premortems, friction, and practical protection that make known failures harder to re-enter.
chapters.coreMove: Put guardrails around a known weakness before the weak condition returns.
chapters.commonMisread: Making safeguards feel fearful, bureaucratic, or abstract rather than practical protection.

chapters.title: How to Handle Mistakes
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter moves from prevention to recovery: repair, reflection, learning loop, and disciplined response when failure still happens.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a mistake into repair and learning before shame or defensiveness freezes it in place.
chapters.commonMisread: Self-forgiveness theater, resilience slogans, or regret loops with no correction.

chapters.title: Define the Problem
chapters.sourcePressure: The decision-process section starts by clarifying the real problem: framing, obstacles, responsibility, and root cause before effort goes toward the wrong target.
chapters.coreMove: Rewrite the complaint into the obstacle you can actually act on.
chapters.commonMisread: Jumping to solutions or importing problem-solving frameworks before the problem is named cleanly.

chapters.title: Explore Possible Solutions
chapters.sourcePressure: After defining the problem, widen the option search: options, possibilities, open search, alternatives, and avoiding early lock-in before evaluation begins.
chapters.coreMove: Generate enough live options that the first plausible answer has to compete.
chapters.commonMisread: Endless brainstorming or creativity talk instead of disciplined option search before comparison.

chapters.title: Evaluate the Options
chapters.sourcePressure: Now compare alternatives through tradeoffs, criteria, information quality, and judgment. Attractive options must be tested against evidence quality and real costs before action.
chapters.coreMove: Make each option stand beside the same criteria so attractiveness cannot outrun evidence.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning evaluation into a scoring spreadsheet or abstract optimization exercise.

chapters.title: Do it!
chapters.sourcePressure: Judged alternatives still fail without execution. This chapter is about commitment, action, follow-through, and resisting hesitation, reopening, and drift after a choice is made.
chapters.coreMove: Convert the chosen option into the next irreversible action before doubt reopens the vote.
chapters.commonMisread: Motivational exhortation or busyness instead of committed follow-through after judgment.

chapters.title: Margin of Safety
chapters.sourcePressure: Action needs protection against uncertainty: slack, buffer, resilience, and practical protection against ordinary error and variance.
chapters.coreMove: Add enough buffer that normal variance cannot turn a good decision into a fragile one.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating margin as pessimism, waste, or financial formula instead of practical resilience.

chapters.title: Learn from Your Decisions
chapters.sourcePressure: Protected action becomes improvement only when outcomes are interpreted carefully: feedback, postmortem, reflection, process, result, and noise.
chapters.coreMove: Separate decision process from outcome noise before updating your rules.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating any good result as proof or any bad result as failure.

chapters.title: Dickens's Hidden Lesson
chapters.sourcePressure: The late-book turn shifts from decision quality to value quality: what matters, hidden costs, miswanting, fulfillment, and whether pursued outcomes are worth wanting.
chapters.coreMove: Audit the hidden costs of a desire before treating achievement as the same thing as fulfillment.
chapters.commonMisread: Literary analysis, anti-ambition sermon, or moral theory instead of practical examination of wanting.

chapters.title: The Happiness Experts
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter tests priorities against hindsight, regret, elder wisdom, life satisfaction, and what later still feels worthwhile.
chapters.coreMove: Let elder hindsight challenge what current ambition is calling important.
chapters.commonMisread: Sentimental advice, pop happiness frameworks, or nostalgia replacing present judgment.

chapters.title: Memento Mori
chapters.sourcePressure: Mortality awareness sharpens hindsight into perspective, clarity, and urgency about what deserves finite life.
chapters.coreMove: Use death awareness to shrink false urgency and reveal what still deserves attention.
chapters.commonMisread: Theatrical gloom, borrowed philosophy costume, or panic-driven living.

chapters.title: Life Lessons from Death
chapters.sourcePressure: The final perspective chapter asks what death reveals about tiny moments, repeated priorities, living well, and what a life finally amounts to.
chapters.coreMove: Judge daily uses of time by the life they are quietly building.
chapters.commonMisread: Vague inspiration, consolation, or saying only small things matter.
